title: Johnny Marzetti
subtitle: Midwestern baked pasta with beef mince, tomato, and melted cheddar
excerpt: A beloved Midwest American casserole of elbow pasta, spiced beef mince, and tinned tomatoes baked under a thick layer of cheddar. Cheap and deeply comforting.
sourceNotes: Ohio Midwest casserole tradition, popularised in the early 20th century and spread through American school and community cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool fully, then freeze in the dish or in portions. Defrost overnight in the fridge. Bake covered at 180C for 25 minutes until hot through, then uncover for 5 minutes to re-melt the cheese.
recipe.batchNotes: Use a larger roasting tin and double the quantities. Works well for feeding a crowd.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the day before, cover, and refrigerate. Add 10 minutes to the bake time when cooking from cold.

content.text: Johnny Marzetti is an American baked pasta casserole from Ohio, layered with seasoned beef mince and a lot of cheddar. Cook the pasta slightly short of done before it goes in the oven. It finishes cooking in the sauce and absorbs the flavour as it bakes.
Heat the oven to 180C. Cook the pasta in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the beef mince and cook for 5 minutes until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the onion, celery, and green pepper. Cook for 5 minutes until the vegetables soften.
Add the garlic, tomato puree, paprika, and oregano. Stir and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes, passata, and Worcestershire sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the drained pasta to the sauce and stir to combine. Tip into a large gratin dish. Scatter the cheddar evenly over the top.
Bake uncovered for 25 minutes until the cheese is golden and the edges are bubbling. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The pasta is mushy after baking.
items.cause: The pasta was fully cooked before going into the oven.
items.fix: Always undercook the pasta by 2 minutes before mixing with the sauce. It finishes in the oven.

items.symptom: The casserole is dry after baking.
items.cause: The sauce was too thick before the pasta was added, or the dish baked uncovered for too long.
items.fix: Add an extra 100ml of passata to the sauce before assembling. Cover with foil for the first 15 minutes if the dish looks dry going in.

items.symptom: The cheese does not brown properly.
items.cause: The oven is not hot enough or the dish is on the wrong shelf.
items.fix: Move the dish to the top third of the oven for the last 5 minutes, or finish under a medium grill for 2 to 3 minutes.
